extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent examiners, patent applicants, and other USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level objectives, standards, and measurable criteria the USPTO uses to ensure high-quality, timely patent examination and to validate its performance reporting (including PTA/PTE calculations, examiner training, quality reviews, AI tools, and trademark controls).

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA/PTE calculation validity and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO uses valid and reliable data to calculate Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) and Patent Term Extension (PTE), but manual data entry may introduce errors; calculations must be in compliance with statutes, regulations, and case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found use of valid/reliable data but recommended controls to reduce manual entry errors; corrective actions include SOPs, software update triggers, and statistical review samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require use of safe harbor form PTO/SB/134 for PTA exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish a notice of proposed rulemaking regarding requiring the use of the 'safe harbor' form PTO/SB/134 to claim the exception under 37 CFR § 1.704(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to standardize claiming the PTA exception and reduce errors or inconsistent practices in claiming exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA-PTE Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) with update triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a PTA-PTE SOP and include the identifying events that necessitate updates to the PTA calculator software, such as changes in regulations, case law, and input from the PTA exception events team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOP should explicitly list events requiring software/ process updates to ensure accurate PTA/PTE calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate e-filing of PTE applications with other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the U.S. Department of Agriculture to determine whether the current e-filing of PTE applications at the USPTO will be an acceptable permanent practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interagency coordination to confirm e-filing processes meet other agencies' requirements for PTE determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of workflow tools for Legal Instrument Examiner managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete a feasibility study regarding the implementation of a workflow process or tool for managers of Legal Instrument Examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study should evaluate implementation options to improve oversight and workflow efficiency for Legal Instrument Examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA calculation manual review SOP based on feedback sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a PTA-PTE SOP that will include the identifying events requiring manual review of the PTA calculation process based on feedback from petitions, public inquiries, internal samplings, and other sources of remedial updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOP should identify which feedback sources and thresholds trigger manual review and how to perform it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistically valid random review of PTA calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the requisite sample size for and manner of conducting a PTA calculation review to provide a statistically valid random review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish sampling methodology and size to permit statistically reliable inferences about PTA calculation accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark controls to enforce U.S. counsel rule
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO lacks controls to effectively enforce the U.S. counsel rule; controls are needed to prevent fraudulent or inaccurate trademark registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement procedural or automated checks to ensure filings comply with the U.S. counsel requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and prevent digitally altered or mocked-up trademark specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved trademark filings have contained digitally altered or mocked-up specimens; USPTO must improve specimen examination to detect such alterations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form working groups and develop improved examiner guidance and tools to identify manipulated specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accurate identification of goods and services in trademark filings
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO did not ensure accurate identification of goods and services; examiners need better guidance and processes to verify identification accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clearer guidance, improved training, and system tools to help examiners confirm correct identification of goods/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive trademark fraud risk strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO lacks a comprehensive fraud risk strategy for trademark filings and needs a documented risk framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document Trademarks’ risk framework including risk profile, goals, and targets via the agency’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) Scorecard, updated quarterly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated query to flag PO boxes and 'care of' addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement an automated query in trademark systems that will identify post office boxes and 'care of' addresses and flag the issue for the assigned examining attorney to take appropriate action under examination rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-level detection to prompt examiner review for potentially problematic addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOP to identify suspicious high-volume attorneys/filings and referral standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft an SOP to identify investigations where an attorney of record appears to be participating in a significant number of suspicious filings; identify the type and amount of evidence necessary for referral to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline and determine the appropriate audience and process for referral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOP should include thresholds, evidence standards, and referral workflows to Enrollment & Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarantine groups of suspicious trademark applications pre-assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a process using the Administrator Console feature in the trademark database systems to identify and quarantine groups of applications with suspicious data for investigation before they are assigned to an examining attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-assignment quarantine to reduce examiner workload on fraudulent/mass filings and improve integrity of assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on 'wide' range of unrelated goods under section 904.01(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide appropriate guidance on what constitutes a 'wide' range of unrelated goods for which an examining attorney should take action under section 904.01(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the standard to reduce examiner inconsistency when evaluating breadth/unrelatedness of goods/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify OTQRT database to enable manager input of quality review data
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the Office of Trademark Quality Review and Training’s (OTQRT) database to create a workflow that will allow managers to input quality review data directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System change to improve timeliness and accuracy of quality review data capture and management oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability for performance data provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers of USPTO programs are responsible for providing performance data and are accountable for ensuring procedures are in place to make data accurate and measurement sources complete and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must implement procedures and controls to maintain data integrity for reported performance indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control of performance data via internal automated edits and cross-checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers monitor and maintain automated systems and databases that collect, track, and store performance indicators; each system incorporates internal program edits to control the accuracy of supporting data, and cross-checks among systems provide assurances of data reasonableness and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use system-level edits, cross-system comparisons, and external expert monitoring to validate data collection methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCFO responsibility for performance monitoring and data quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The OCFO is responsible for monitoring the agency’s performance, providing direction on and support for data collection methodology and analysis, ensuring that data quality checks are in place, and reporting performance management data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central oversight role to maintain consistency and rigor in performance reporting across USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic verification and validation of performance measures
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO verifies and validates performance measures periodically to ensure quality, reliability, and credibility; sampling techniques and sample counts are reviewed and adjusted to ensure statistical reliability for making inferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and adjust sampling plans at the start of each fiscal year and at intervals during reporting periods; conduct data analyses to identify statistically significant trends and underlying factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA statutory timeframes (pendency standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory time frames (PTA compliance) are: 14 months from filing to first office action; 4 months to respond to an amendment (including RCE); 4 months to act on a PTAB decision; 4 months to issue a patent after payment of issue fee; 36 months from filing to issue date of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets set to achieve 90% within these statutory time frames; agency measures mailed actions and remaining inventory PTA compliance against these timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA compliance targets and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2021, USPTO set targets to achieve total PTA statutory compliance for 84% of mailed actions and 86% of remaining inventory; actual results: total PTA compliance for mailed actions 83%, for remaining inventory 86%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total PTA Compliance is computed as weighted average of PTA categories; track per-category compliance (table provided) and overall weighted compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate efficiency via cost per patent production unit
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO evaluates the efficiency of the patent examination process by measuring total patent-related expenses compared with patent production to calculate cost per patent production unit over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical fiscal year cost-per-unit tracking and targets to assess cost-effectiveness of resource application to production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage international worksharing (PPH, PCT, Global Dossier)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and optimize worksharing programs (Patent Prosecution Highway, PCT programs, Global Dossier) to increase efficiencies and decrease costs for applicants filing in multiple offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue stewardship and pilot collaborative search programs to enhance predictability and reliability of IP rights worldwide; Global Dossier provides single access to related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer additional prosecution options to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and provide prosecution options (e.g., Track One Prioritized Examination, Quick Path IDS, After Final Consideration Pilot 2.0, COVID-19 Prioritized Examination Pilot, Patents 4 Patients, PPH) to advance application progress and assist applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs have eligibility requirements and may expedite examination (e.g., Track One goal: examination within 12 months of filing); USPTO explores additional targeted programs (e.g., climate-related acceleration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase examiners' ability to obtain best prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance examiners' access to prior art through deployment of advanced technology solutions (new patent search system and experts for search strategies), improving quality and timeliness of examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tools, training, and access to extensive foreign patent documents and machine translations; emphasize searching inventive concept early in prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and roll out PE2E Search with AI capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PE2E Search provides advanced search functionalities and integrates AI capabilities to help examiners identify relevant documents and suggest additional areas to search; rollout began to examiners and a limited public version is planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool learns from examiner feedback; public version to be limited initially; transparency features to help examiners interpret AI results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and test Deferred Subject Matter Eligibility Response Pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a pilot program to determine whether delaying full examination of subject matter eligibility issues until other patentability deficiencies are resolved could improve examination efficiency and patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot to assess whether compact prosecution principles could be adjusted across technology areas; informed by stakeholder input and congressional letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and improve examiner technical and legal training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training via a collaborative Patent Training Council, Refresher Training Program, Master Class Program, PETTP, VILT, and STEPP to maintain or expand examiners' procedural, legal, communication, and automation skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should be legally compliant, consistent, structured to maximize learning, and extended to external stakeholders; virtual delivery increases accessibility including international STEPP offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Master Review Form (MRF) to evaluate patent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA reviews random samples of examiner work products using the Master Review Form, which includes over 20 unique sections and over 330 inquiries, to capture compliance with title 35 and relevant case law at time of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews allow identification of quality trends and corrective measures (e.g., training); MRF also captures best practices and accolades-worthy work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent compliance indicator goals for statutes (101,102,103,112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals: >97% compliance for 35 U.S.C. §101; >95% for §102; >93% for §103; >93% for §112. Actual FY2021 results provided (98.3%, 95.1%, 90.7%, 92.2%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these statutory compliance indicators to measure correctness of office actions and to target areas for improvement where actual falls short of goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accolades program for exemplary examiner work
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA designates instances of high-quality examiner work as accolades for work that generally goes beyond basic MPEP requirements, often recognizing best practices, clear writing, and excellent customer service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accolade-worthy work receives recognition (letter from OPQA Director); approximately 15.6% of reviewed work received accolades in FY2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: External customer surveys to validate quality perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Semiannual external surveys sent to approximately 3,000 frequent filers capture perceptions on adherence to rules, correctness/clarity/consistency of rejections, and overall examination quality; satisfaction trends monitored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey results used to validate internal quality findings; prior art rejections under §§102/103 are key drivers of overall quality perception; track ratios of Good/Excellent to Poor/Very Poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine production standards for examiner time allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise time allotted for examiners to examine applications, including increased base/minimum time and additional time for applications exceeding thresholds (number of claims, specification length, IDS pages), and factor in an application's classification 'picture'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make allotments transparent and flexible; adjust as conditions change to maintain time needed for quality and to balance pendency, cost, and quality objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Route applications to examiners based on technological profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Route applications more effectively by matching each application's unique technological profile with patent examiner experience to assign applications to examiners with requisite expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve application-examiner matching to enhance search quality and examination efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner performance appraisal emphasizing best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated examiner performance appraisal plan provides a roadmap with exemplary practices in search, clarity of written prosecution record, and principles of compact prosecution; emphasizes searching the inventive concept early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appraisal plan should guide performance evaluation and training priorities, focusing on behaviors that promote patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop AI auto-classification with explainability and feedback integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Auto-classification tool leverages ML to suggest CPC symbols, identify claimed subject matter for refinement, and link suggested CPC symbols to specific portions of the document to provide insight into AI reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate enhanced feedback mechanisms with existing classification processes to train the AI; auto-classification implemented for internal operations to identify claimed subject matter with CPC and reduce expenditures on CPC data acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture examiner feedback to improve AI search tools
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-based search system is configured to automatically capture feedback data from examiners to yield further enhancements over time and includes features to help examiners interpret AI-generated results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for learning from users and transparency so examiners can use AI suggestions effectively and understand rationale behind suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot and staged rollout for AI features
rubrics_metrics.description: Beta versions of AI search tools should be released to subsets of examiners for assessment and refinement prior to agency-wide rollout; first AI search feature scheduled for release to entire corps after testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use phased deployments and refine based on user feedback and performance analyses before full deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain and onboard examiners via virtual training and nationwide hiring
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Training Academy onboarded and trained new employees virtually, enabling expansion of a nationwide workforce; in FY2021, hired 492 utility/reissue and 46 design examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize virtual training for interactivity and community connectivity; leverage telework programs to retain talent without relocation.
